themes.label: Treaties and Agreements
themes.rationale: The inscription explicitly identifies itself as a treaty between the Gortynians and the Knossians.

themes.label: Decrees
themes.rationale: The text uses the standard decree formula 'it seemed good to the city' and mentions the voting of the three hundred.
themes.quote: [τάδ ἔδοξε τᾶι πόλι] ψαφίξανσι τρι[ακ]ατίων παρ[ιόντων]

themes.label: Calendars and Timetables
themes.rationale: The treaty is dated by local months and specific days, and it sets deadlines for the implementation of its terms.
themes.quote: μη]νὸς Ἱονιω ἠν[άτα καὶ δεκάται ... μη]-νὸς Καρνήιω ἠνάται καὶ δ[εκάται]

themes.label: Accounts and Financial Records
themes.rationale: The inscription contains detailed provisions regarding the repayment of loans, guarantees, and the return of gold and silver property.
themes.quote: δάνεια ἢ ἐνγύας ὀφήλει ἁ πόλις ἁ τῶν Κν[ωσίων ... ἢ χρυσία ἢ ἀργύρια ἢ ἄλλο [τι ἀποδιδόναι]

themes.label: Religious and Dedicatory Texts
themes.rationale: The treaty mentions the restoration of property or status to the goddess Athena.
themes.ambiguity_note: The specific nature of the restoration to Athena is partially lost in the lacuna.

rationale: This inscription records a peace treaty between the Cretan cities of Gortyn and Knossos, mediated by King Ptolemy. The text outlines the cessation of hostilities, the return of property (including gold and silver), the restoration of the territory of Apollonia, and the settlement of public and private debts. It is dated by the local magistrates and months of both cities.
